newsitem.title: USA: Latin debts calm, Bulgaria up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Latin debts calm, Bulgaria up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Latin Bradies were mostly flat in slow trade, while Bulgaria bounced from Thursday's slump on bargain-hunting, market sources said.
"There has not been much liquidity in the last 10 days," said a Latin Brady trader.
With the U.S. Treasuries treading water at the moment, the emerging market debts followed by bobbing up and down at about the same spot, he said.
Par bonds on the whole performed better than discounts, reflecting expectations that U.S. interest rates would stay low, traders said.
Venezuela papers, which had been hot until recently, appeared to suffer from buyer fatigue, they said.
Venezuela PARs VZ675C20=RR and FLIRBs VZ6C97=RR were unchanged at 74-3/4 and 86-1/8, while DCBs VZFLL07=RR were bid 1/4 higher at 85 even.
On the other hand, there was a friendly tone to Ecuador bonds on hopes that a currency convertibility plan would be adopted, even though the long-awaited economic plan was postponed to December 1.
"The delay is not a bad sign," said James Barrineau, emerging market strategist at Smith Barney. "It is going to be a comprehensive plan that will include a currency board."
A currency board to peg the Ecuadorian sucre to the dollar would enhance the attractiveness of the local currency market and boost the dollar debts as well, he said.
The Bulgarian debts took a breather after being pounded on Thursday. The lev, which had plunged 30 percent in the week, steadied, albeit precariously.
The chance that Bulgaria would adopt a currency board to restore investors' confidence is even higher than in Ecuador, said Barrineau. "It will bow to the IMF's wishes," he said.

The IMF mission in Sofia endorses the currency board, saying in a statement on Friday: "The stability of financial markets under a currency board would likely result in an increase in confidence in the securities market."
Bulgaria IAB BGFLTH=RR, which lost two points on Thursday, recouped 1-1/8 to 47-1/8 bid.
Russia's Vnesh loans and Minfin bonds softened in the wake of Thursday's Eurobond-inspired rally.
"We think it's a great opportunity to hop on the moving train," said a trader, who especially favored the Minfins.
Russia dollar-denominated Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR lost 1/2 to bid 78-5/8 and MinFin 3 RU3E99=RR slipped 3/8 to bid 83-3/8.
